quick.summary: How to stop broken records from ruining your final tables.
quick.takeaway: Test your data before passing it on so mistakes stay contained.

beats.line: My chart showed ten million sales today. How did fake numbers get past me?
You served the meal without tasting the soup.
I just passed the tables along as soon as they updated.
Right. If you add salt, you taste it before taking it out to diners.
We do this with pipelines using data anomaly detection.
Can I just call it a quality check?
You test if a column is empty, or if a number is completely crazy.
If the check fails, the pipeline stops before anyone sees the mess.
The soup stays in the kitchen until it is right.

quiz.question: What is the main reason to use a quality check in your pipeline?
options: To stop bad data before anyone sees it.
To make the job run much faster.
To tell you what the column means.
quiz.explanation: A quality check catches bad numbers early, preventing them from ruining reports downstream.

quiz.question: A quality check should only happen at the very end of your project.
quiz.explanation: You should check data at various steps along the pipeline, just like tasting food while cooking.
